```{r install edgeR}
BiocManager::install("DESeq2")
```

# Load library 
# edgeR version 3.38.0
```{r}
library(edgeR)
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Get count dataset
```{r}
count_matrix <- as.matrix(read.delim("/home/newol210/macknight_oliver/NoneVsHigh_RNASeq_2023/Illumina_downloads_2023/RSEM_trinity_matrix_files/RSEM.gene.counts.matrix", header = TRUE, row.names = 1))
```

```{r}
head(count_matrix, 10)
```

```{r}
count_matrix <- round(count_matrix[,], digits = 0)
head(count_matrix, 5)
```

```{r}
sample_info <- c("ctr", "ctr", "ctr", "ctr", "ctr", "trt", "trt", "trt", "trt", "trt")
```

# Create DGEList data class for count and sample information
```{r}
dge <- DGEList(counts = count_matrix, group = factor(sample_info))
dge
```

# Filter out geneIDs with low counts
```{r}
keep <- filterByExpr(y = dge)
dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes=FALSE]
```

# calcNormFactors function is used for TMM normalization and calculating normalization (scaling) factors
```{r}
dge <- calcNormFactors(object = dge)
```

# Model fitting and estimating dispersions
# edgeR internally calculates pseudo count for speeding up the analysis for negative binomial (NB) dispersion estimation and exact test for pairwise comparison
# estimateDisp() function estimates both common and tagwise dispersions in one run
```{r}
dge <- estimateDisp(y = dge)
```

# The exact test (exact p values) is used for testing the differential expression of genes between two condition counts data
```{r}
et <- exactTest(object = dge)
```

# topTags() function is useful to extract the table with adjusted p values (FDR; false discovery rate). The output table is ordered by p values
# Comparison of groups:  trt-ctr (meaning the positive logFC represents the gene is more highly expressed in the trt condition as compared to the ctr condition and vice versa)
```{r}
top_degs = topTags(object = et, n = "Inf")
top_degs
```

# Get a summary DGE table (returns significant genes with absolute log fold change at least 1 and adjusted p value < 0.05)
```{r}
summary(decideTests(object = et, lfc = 1))
```

```{r}
sig_genes <- top_degs[top_degs$table$FDR < 0.05 & abs(top_degs$table$logFC) > 1,]
```

```{r}
sig_genes
```

```{r}
write.csv(as.data.frame(sig_genes), file="/home/newol210/macknight_oliver/NoneVsHigh_RNASeq_2023/Illumina_downloads_2023/RSEM_trinity_matrix_files/EdgeR_de_novo_SIG_dge.csv")
```

```{r}
write.csv(as.data.frame(top_degs), file="/Volumes/olivernewman/2023/EdgeR_outputs/De_novo_mapping_sigDEGs/EdgeR_de_novo_dge.csv")
```

```{r}
plotMD(object = et)
```

```{r}
plot(et$table$logFC, -10*log10(et$table$PValue), main="Volcano plot", xlab="log(FC)", ylab="-log10(P-val)")
```

# Second volcano plot
```{r}
volcano_df <- transform(
  et$table,
  negLogP = -log10(PValue),
  Significant = PValue < 0.05 & abs(logFC) > 1
)

p_volcano <- ggplot(volcano_df, aes(x = logFC, y = negLogP)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Significant), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("grey70", "firebrick")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = expression(log[2]~Fold~Change),
    y = expression(-log[10]~P~value)
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_volcano

ggsave(
  "/home/newol210/macknight_oliver/NoneVsHigh_RNASeq_2023/Illumina_downloads_2023/RSEM_trinity_matrix_files/Volcano_RSEM_2023.svg",
  p_volcano,
  width = 6,
  height = 5)
```

# Plot PCA
```{r}
# Convert edgeR object to DESeq2 object for PCA plot
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = count_matrix, colData = data.frame(sample_info), design = ~sample_info)
vsd <- vst(dds, blind=FALSE)

# PCA plot
p_pca <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = "sample_info") +
  theme_minimal()

p_pca

ggsave(
  "/home/newol210/macknight_oliver/NoneVsHigh_RNASeq_2023/Illumina_downloads_2023/RSEM_trinity_matrix_files/PCA_RSEM_2023.svg",
  p_pca,
  width = 6,
  height = 5)

# Explanation:
# 1. **Loading Libraries**: Added `library(DESeq2)` and `library(ggplot2)` for PCA plotting.
# 2. **Convert to DESeq2 Object**: Converted `count_matrix` to a `DESeq2` object.
# 3. **Variance Stabilizing Transformation**: Applied `vst` (variance stabilizing transformation) to the `DESeq2` object.
# 4. **PCA Plot**: Created the PCA plot using `plotPCA` and `ggplot2` functions.
# This script should now generate a PCA plot as part of the RNA-Seq differential expression analysis.
```

# The following is for seeing what genes are causing separation on PC2 amoung sample-sets
```{r}
# Ensure DESeq2 and edgeR libraries are loaded

# Assuming vsd is already created from DESeq2 object
# Perform PCA
pca <- prcomp(t(assay(vsd)))

# Check the structure of the PCA result
str(pca)

# Extract the loadings for PC2
loadings <- pca$rotation[, 2]

# Ensure loadings are correctly extracted
head(loadings)

# Check the length of the loadings
length(loadings)

# Sort loadings by absolute value to find the most influential genes on PC2
sorted_indices <- order(abs(loadings), decreasing = TRUE)

# Check if the sorting was successful
head(sorted_indices)

# Get the names of the genes sorted by their influence on PC2
top_gene_names <- rownames(pca$rotation)[sorted_indices]

# Ensure the names are correctly extracted
head(top_gene_names)

# Get the corresponding loadings for these genes
top_gene_loadings <- loadings[sorted_indices]

# Ensure loadings match the gene names
head(top_gene_loadings)

# Create a data frame to view the top genes and their loadings
top_gene_df <- data.frame(Gene = top_gene_names, Loading = top_gene_loadings)

# View the top genes driving PC2
head(top_gene_df)
```
